S.FORM: tia=ku pu-a-isua naini vanai tamu pa-ta-ŋanai-ini tamu kisa-ən.
S.PHON: tiaku puaisua naini vanai tamu pataŋanaiini tamu kisaən
S.FORM: tiaku puaisua naini vanai tamu patanganaiini tamu kisaen.
S.PHON: tiaku puaisua naini vanai tamu pataŋanaiini tamu kisaen
S.TRANSL: I want to talk about the reason why the hundred-pacer snake is called tamu.

S.FORM: miana, miana ʔuna ta-cini maanu saruanai nanala. ʔakia tanasa-ini, paira tia=kilimi ʔaravaŋ tu-ʔuna-ini si-a-ʔicəpə.
S.PHON: miana miana ʔuna tatʂini maanu saruanai nanaɾa ʔakia tanasaini paira tiakiɾimi ʔaravaŋ tuʔunaini ʂiaʔiʦəpə
S.FORM: miana, miana 'una tacini maanu saruanai nanara. 'akia tanasaini, paira tiakirimi 'aravang tu'unaini sia'icepe.
S.PHON: miana miana ʔuna tatʂini maanu sa[r|ɾ]uanai nana[r|ɾ]a ʔakia tanasaini pai[r|ɾ]a tiaki[r|ɾ]imi ʔa[r|ɾ]avaŋ tuʔunaini ʂiaʔiʦepe
S.TRANSL: Once upon a time, there was a boy who was an orphan. He didn't have his house and often looked for a cave to sleep in.

S.FORM: ʔuna u-cani taniarə ni-m-ətəa ʔaravaŋ tatia, pa-cəpə-cəpəŋ ŋuain, "tia=ku ala-vali naisi ma-sətaanə ma-manəŋə."
S.PHON: ʔuna uʦani taniarə nimətəa ʔaravaŋ tatia paʦəpəʦəpəŋ ŋuain tiaku aɾavaɾi naiʂi masətaanə mamanəŋə
S.FORM: 'una ucani taniare nimetea 'aravang tatia, pacepecepeng nguain, "tiaku aravari naisi masetaane mamanenge."
S.PHON: ʔuna uʦani tania[r|ɾ]e nimetea ʔa[r|ɾ]avaŋ tatia paʦepeʦepeŋ ŋuain tiaku a[r|ɾ]ava[r|ɾ]i naiʂi masetaane mamaneŋe
S.TRANSL: One day, he found a large cave and thought to himself, "It will be best for me to move here."

S.FORM: makasua=cu um-ala ŋuain tamna nua-nuamani pasa-vali na ʔaravaŋ tatia.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu umaɾa ŋuain tamna nuanuamani pasavaɾi na ʔaravaŋ tatia
S.FORM: makasuacu umara nguain tamna nuanuamani pasavari na 'aravang tatia.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu uma[r|ɾ]a ŋuain tamna nuanuamani pasava[r|ɾ]i na ʔa[r|ɾ]avaŋ tatia
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, he took his belongings and moved into the large cave.

S.FORM: kau=cu mia-ranau ʔacu ŋuain ma-pitəʔə, muun=cu ʔinia maanu saruanai mu-taruʔan.
S.PHON: kauʦu miaranau ʔaʦu ŋuain mapitəʔə muunʦu ʔinia maanu saruanai mutaruʔan
S.FORM: kaucu miaranau 'acu nguain mapite'e, muuncu 'inia maanu saruanai mutaru'an.
S.PHON: kauʦu mia[r|ɾ]anau ʔaʦu ŋuain mapiteʔe muunʦu ʔinia maanu sa[r|ɾ]uanai muta[r|ɾ]uʔan
S.TRANSL: Before long it became dark, and the boy stayed there overnight.

S.FORM: vərəŋana=cu t<um>a-timana ʔuna riaŋ mu-sikar-a na təək-ini. timana=kiai ma-kaitia tamu nanakə tamna riaŋ.
S.PHON: vərəŋanaʦu tumatimana ʔuna riaŋ muʂikara na təəkini timanakiai makaitia tamu nanakə tamna riaŋ
S.FORM: verenganacu t<um>atimana 'una riang musikara na teekini. timanakiai makaitia tamu nanake tamna riang.
S.PHON: ve[r|ɾ]eŋanaʦu tumatimana ʔuna [r|ɾ]iaŋ muʂika[r|ɾ]a na teekini timanakiai makaitia tamu nanake tamna [r|ɾ]iaŋ
S.TRANSL: Late at night, he heard a sound reaching his ears, and it sounded much like a grandmother's voice to him.

S.FORM: ma-kari na maanu nanala t<um>a-tuturu ʔinia, "ʔakuni ma-ʔicəpə. ʔapacuʔ-ai ʔaravaŋ tu-ʔuna=musu iisi ma-pitəʔə, ʔakuni ma-ʔicəpə si tia=cu mia-cara kasua."
S.PHON: makari na maanu nanaɾa tumatuturu ʔinia ʔakuni maʔiʦəpə ʔapaʦuʔai ʔaravaŋ tuʔunamusu iiʂi mapitəʔə ʔakuni maʔiʦəpə ʂi tiaʦu miaʦara kasua
S.FORM: makari na maanu nanara t<um>atuturu 'inia, "'akuni ma'icepe. 'apacu'ai 'aravang tu'unamusu iisi mapite'e, 'akuni ma'icepe si tiacu miacara kasua."
S.PHON: maka[r|ɾ]i na maanu nana[r|ɾ]a tumatutu[r|ɾ]u ʔinia ʔakuni maʔiʦepe ʔapaʦuʔai ʔa[r|ɾ]avaŋ tuʔunamusu iiʂi mapiteʔe ʔakuni maʔiʦepe ʂi tiaʦu miaʦa[r|ɾ]a kasua
S.TRANSL: It said to the orphan, "Don't be afraid. Although the cave you're staying in is dark, don't be afraid because I'll take care of you."

S.FORM: makasua=cu ara-ʔakia=cu riaŋ tamu.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu araʔakiaʦu riaŋ tamu
S.FORM: makasuacu ara'akiacu riang tamu.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu a[r|ɾ]aʔakiaʦu [r|ɾ]iaŋ tamu
S.TRANSL: Then, there was no more sound of the grandmother's voice.

S.FORM: ara-ciasə=cu ta-sikar-a ʔaravaŋ sua nanala, ʔuna u-cani tamu vunai t<in>ələkə-ləkə.
S.PHON: aratʂiasəʦu taʂikara ʔaravaŋ sua nanaɾa ʔuna uʦani tamu vunai tinəɾəkəɾəkə
S.FORM: araciasecu tasikara 'aravang sua nanara, 'una ucani tamu vunai t<in>erekereke.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]atʂiaseʦu taʂika[r|ɾ]a ʔa[r|ɾ]avaŋ sua nana[r|ɾ]a ʔuna uʦani tamu vunai tine[r|ɾ]eke[r|ɾ]eke
S.TRANSL: At dawn, the orphan looked deep into the cave and saw a hundred-pacer snake coiled up.

S.FORM: sua navuŋ-ini ia, ʔaisi və-vəcəkai, m-ali-sələ-sələcə ʔavacə makai tia=ma-kari ʔikua, "ʔakuni ma-ʔicəpə ʔikua. kaʔan=ku tia=r<um>a-raʔisi kasua. mu-ʔuna naisi, tia=kita tu-taŋlia."
S.PHON: sua navuŋini ia ʔaiʂi vəvəʦəkai maɾisəɾəsəɾəʦə ʔavaʦə makai tiamakari ʔikua ʔakuni maʔiʦəpə ʔikua kaʔanku tiarumaraʔiʂi kasua muʔuna naiʂi tiakita tutaŋɾia
S.FORM: sua navungini ia, 'aisi vevecekai, marisereserece 'avace makai tiamakari 'ikua, "'akuni ma'icepe 'ikua. ka'anku tiar<um>ara'isi kasua. mu'una naisi, tiakita tutangria."
S.PHON: sua navuŋini ia ʔaiʂi veveʦekai ma[r|ɾ]ise[r|ɾ]ese[r|ɾ]eʦe ʔavaʦe makai tiamaka[r|ɾ]i ʔikua ʔakuni maʔiʦepe ʔikua kaʔanku tia[r|ɾ]uma[r|ɾ]aʔiʂi kasua muʔuna naiʂi tiakita tutaŋ[r|ɾ]ia
S.TRANSL: The snake's head was in the center, flicking its tongue as if it were telling me, "Don't be afraid of me. I won't bite you. Since we're living here, we'll be friends."

S.FORM: makasua=cu maanu nanala tan-taniarə muun=cu na ʔaravaŋ tatia mata-lava=na tu-nanmanluan.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu maanu nanaɾa tantaniarə muunʦu na ʔaravaŋ tatia mataɾavana tunanmanɾuan
S.FORM: makasuacu maanu nanara tantaniare muuncu na 'aravang tatia mataravana tunanmanruan.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu maanu nana[r|ɾ]a tantania[r|ɾ]e muunʦu na ʔa[r|ɾ]avaŋ tatia mata[r|ɾ]avana tunanman[r|ɾ]uan
S.TRANSL: The orphan stayed in the large cave every day until he became a young man.

S.FORM: aranai=cu mia-sua pa-ta-ŋanai-ini vunai tamu misa "tamu" kisa-ən.
S.PHON: aranaiʦu miasua pataŋanaiini vunai tamu misa tamu kisaən
S.FORM: aranaicu miasua patanganaiini vunai tamu misa "tamu" kisaen.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]anaiʦu miasua pataŋanaiini vunai tamu misa tamu kisaen
S.TRANSL: Since then, the hundred-pacer snake was named tamu meaning 'grandparent'.

S.FORM: makasua aranai miana ma-maaraŋ ia, makasua t<um>a-tuturu a-pa-tuntunu mata-lava=cu masini-a.
S.PHON: makasua aranai miana mamaaraŋ ia makasua tumatuturu apatuntunu mataɾavaʦu maʂinia
S.FORM: makasua aranai miana mamaarang ia, makasua t<um>atuturu apatuntunu mataravacu masinia.
S.PHON: makasua a[r|ɾ]anai miana mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ ia makasua tumatutu[r|ɾ]u apatuntunu mata[r|ɾ]avaʦu maʂinia
S.TRANSL: In that way, this story has been passed down from the elders in the past to the present.

S.FORM: sua iisi ia, pə-ʔə-ʔəna pu-a-isua vunai tamu.
S.PHON: sua iiʂi ia pəʔəʔəna puaisua vunai tamu
S.FORM: sua iisi ia, pe'e'ena puaisua vunai tamu.
S.PHON: sua iiʂi ia peʔeʔena puaisua vunai tamu
S.TRANSL: This is the story of the hundred-pacer snake.
